memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he sent young Israelite men, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as fellowship offerings to the Lord." - Exodus 24:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the covenant could be sealed, sacrifices had to be made. Two kinds are mentioned here. Burnt offerings were entirely consumed — nothing held back, everything given wholly to God. Fellowship offerings, by contrast, were shared, celebrating peace and communion between God and His people. Together they say something profound: relationship with God involves both complete surrender and joyful fellowship.

Notice that both were necessary. Approaching a holy God was never a casual matter; blood had to be shed. But the goal was never merely appeasement — it was fellowship, friendship, peace with God. The sacrifices were not the end but the doorway into relationship with Him. God has always wanted His people near.

Every one of these offerings pointed forward to Christ. He is our burnt offering, giving Himself wholly and holding nothing back for our sake. And He is our peace, the one through whom we now have true fellowship with God (Rom 5:1; Eph 2:14). The animals had to be repeated year after year; Jesus offered Himself once for all (Heb 10:10). Because of Him, we do not approach God clutching our own sacrifices, but resting in His finished work. What remains for us is grateful surrender — offering ourselves wholly to the One who gave everything for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I holding anything back from God, or is my surrender wholehearted?
Do I live in the joy of true fellowship and peace with God through Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You gave Yourself wholly for me and made me at peace with God. In grateful response, help me hold nothing back but offer my whole life to You. Amen.
